requirements_slice.system_goal: Rerun backend active-slice strict-GRACE canon sync after the cancelled architect/planner attempt, keeping packet-local implementation evidence separate from the final canonical backend observability lane.

in_scope.item: Add and align strict-GRACE module contracts, module maps, function contracts, and semantic START/END blocks for backend/app/main.py, backend/app/logging_utils.py, backend/app/middleware/correlation.py, backend/app/services/day_brief.py, backend/app/services/day_brief_validators.py, backend/app/services/week_brief_service.py, backend/app/services/scheduler.py, and backend/app/services/analytics.py.

Reuse the existing backend active-slice module boundaries across M-API-GATEWAY, M-TRACE-LOGGING, M-DAY-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-WEEK-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-ANALYTICS-EVENTS, and M-OPS-AUTOMATION unless implementation discovers a concrete scope conflict.

Keep packet-local evidence ownership limited to backend quick, targeted active-slice tests, and read-only post-test review, while reserving canonical today-week observability for the final verifier lane.

out_of_scope.item: Do not change Day, Week, report-read, scheduler, or analytics business semantics.
Do not perform a maximal logging rewrite or middleware redesign.

use_case.summary: Resume the backend active-slice canon-sync wave with explicit evidence-lane ownership and implementation-ready bounded write scope.
use_case.scenario: The bounded backend active-slice files expose explicit module contracts, module maps, and stable semantic blocks aligned with local strict-GRACE style.
Exported and orchestration entrypoints in the touched backend files keep or gain function contracts only where the local style requires them.
The implementation wave can be verified with packet-local backend/read-only evidence without claiming canonical today-week closeout.
The final verifier lane owns canonical today-week observability and records an explicit verdict for the touched active-slice flows.

business_invariants.invariant: Canon-sync edits may tighten strict-GRACE addressability only; they must not change DayBrief, WeekBrief, report-read, scheduler, analytics, or correlation header business semantics.

The active slice continues to span M-API-GATEWAY, M-TRACE-LOGGING, M-DAY-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-WEEK-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-ANALYTICS-EVENTS, and M-OPS-AUTOMATION; correlation middleware remains a child of the trace/logging slice rather than a standalone business slice.
Packet-local evidence and wave-final canonical observability are separate lanes: W01 owns read-only packet-local review, and W02 owns today-week canonical closeout.
Existing inline request-correlation binding in backend/app/main.py may remain in place for this rerun unless a concrete implementation blocker requires consolidation on CorrelationIdMiddleware.

expected_failure_handling.item: If a target backend file cannot be aligned to the local strict-GRACE style without semantic risk, preserve behavior and document the remaining gap instead of widening the refactor.
If backend quick and targeted tests pass but read-only evidence is not attributable by module/function/block naming, W01 remains incomplete until markers or evidence notes are corrected.
If W02 canonical today-week evidence is absent, fragmented, or unexpectedly degraded, the rerun wave remains blocked even if W01 packet-local gates passed.

known_defects.defect: The existing rerun slice docs under docs/backend-active-slice-grace-canon-sync-rerun were scaffold-level placeholders and did not capture the required active module set, evidence-lane split, or implementation-ready wave boundaries.

success_criteria.criterion: Backend active slice is formally addressable by module/function/block.
Packet-local gates use packet-local evidence only.
Final verifier lane owns the canonical backend runtime observability gate and records a clean, degraded-but-expected, unexpected-degradation, or no-evidence-blocker verdict.
docker exec astro-project-backend-1 python3 scripts/pipeline.py remains green.
Planner handoff has bounded write scope, frozen scope, and separate W01 implementation versus W02 final-verification responsibilities.
